title: Towards Universal Sequence Representation Learning for Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Effective sequential recommenders require sequence representation learning to model historical user behaviors.

gap.claim: Existing sequence representation learning methods explicitly model item IDs, which limits transfer to new recommendation scenarios.

contributions.claim: UniSRec uses item description text to learn transferable item representations across recommendation scenarios.

The approach uses parametric whitening and a mixture-of-experts enhanced adaptor for universal item encoding, plus two contrastive pre-training tasks with multi-domain negatives for universal sequence representation learning.
The pre-trained universal sequence representation model supports parameter-efficient transfer to new recommendation domains or platforms under inductive or transductive settings.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present UniSRec as a novel universal sequence representation learning approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach.
The approach is reported to improve performance in a cross-platform setting, indicating strong transferability.
The code and pre-trained model are reported as available through the linked repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommenders use sequence representation learning to model historical user behaviors.
Methods based on explicit item IDs have limited transferability to new recommendation scenarios.
UniSRec learns transferable item and sequence representations using item text, specialized item encoding, and contrastive pre-training.
The pre-trained model transfers to new domains or platforms in inductive and transductive settings with parameter-efficient adaptation.
The authors report effectiveness on real-world datasets and performance improvement in cross-platform transfer.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not detail the transfer procedure, parameter-efficiency requirements, or differences between inductive and transductive settings.
